text:
zara: hi team, second day and hitting a few roadblocks for obs on the private-embedter service. Datadog lets me view dashboards but creating monitors returns 403; Grafana alerting UI shows but when I try to create an alert it errors with "missing service account"; Sentry DSN not in our vault. who owns service accounts and DSN provisioning?

devex-bot: welcome! quick checklist: 1) ask infra to provision a service account or add you to eng-observability 2) request Grafana folder Editor+Alerting 3) open infra ticket for Sentry slug. docs: https://redwood.internal/obs/quickstart :robot_face:

mike: hey @zara  for Datadog the 403 usually means your API/app key pair lacks monitors_write or you don’t have an app key at all. you can either use the web UI (if you have monitors_write) or create a short-lived monitor under someone else’s app key. example curl to create a monitor (replace keys):
```
curl -s -X POST "https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/monitor" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "DD-API-KEY: $DD_API_KEY" \n  -H "DD-APPLICATION-KEY: $DD_APP_KEY" \n  -d '{"name":"test: private-embedter latency","type":"metric alert","query":"avg(last_1m):avg:private.embed.latency{env:prod} > 750","message":"@pagerduty test monitor","tags":["team:private-embedter"]}'
```
I can run that for you and tag it team:private-embedter to check routing.

grafana-admin: the "missing service account" error in Grafana means the folder alerting backend expects a service account for automated alert provisioning (we require it for private clusters). we maintain a small pool of service accounts per team. file an infra ticket to request either: a) add your user to the existing team service account ACL or b) provision a new service account. include folder uid and desired role.

dd-admin: one gotcha: if you use someone else’s app key for testing, we recommend deleting test monitors after validation and rotating the monitor endpoint tag to the real team tag later. also confirm the channel mapping: folder tag -> slack channel mapping is stored in infra config.

zara: folder UID is `kL8m_v2B`. mike please run the test monitor, and infra-bot I’ll open a ticket for service account access + Sentry slug `private-embedter-zara`.

infra-bot: ticket OBS-4210 created. required fields missing: please include service repo path, org email domain, and envs. Use template obs-onboard-sa to pre-fill. ETA ~2 business days. add `urgent` label to expedite. link: https://redwood.internal/infra/new?template=obs-onboard-sa

mike: created the test monitor and fired a test alert. it routed to #private-embedter-alerts. zara, confirm you saw it.

zara: saw it 44d thanks! grafana-admin, after infra adds me to the service account ACL do I need a special token to programmatically create alerts?

grafana-admin: yes  infra will add the service account to the folder ACL and create a short-lived signed token for API use. token scopes: dashboards:write, alerts:write. tokens rotate every 7 days for private clusters; infra will note rotation policy in the ticket.

zara: perfect. one more: we want to embed a Grafana panel in an internal runbook but need auth to allow the runbook to render for on-call. recommended approach?

grafana-admin: two options: 1) signed iframe embed scoped to the runbook page (short-lived) 2) create a service-account-based signed image snapshot stored in our artifact store (longer lived). for on-call runbooks we usually do signed iframe for live data. include confluence page id in OBS-4210.

devex-bot: pro tip: include the folder UID, dashboard UID, confluence page id, and desired token TTL in your infra ticket to avoid back-and-forth.

zara: updated OBS-4210 with repo, email domain, envs, and confluence page id. thanks everyone for the quick turnaround :heart:
